connections.why: Turing's 1950 paper answered "the mathematical objection", that Gödel's theorem limits machines and not minds, by replying that no one had proved minds free of such limits.
Gödel announced incompleteness at Königsberg on 7 September 1930; the next day, in the same city, Hilbert said "we must know, we will know", and the second theorem ended his programme as he meant it.
Gödel's unprovable sentence is built by the diagonal construction Cantor used to show the real numbers cannot be listed.
